A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 39-page versions of the same Rec-R1 paper. Pages 2–39 match exactly in extracted text and rendered appearance, including the references and Appendices A–G.

before.justification: v3 reports original Rec-R1 experiments on product search, sequential recommendation and product re-ranking in Tables 1–4, with further evaluations and analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the recommendation experiments, generalization evaluations, supplementary comparisons and case studies.

M1.justification: The closed-loop LLM/recommender framework, GRPO optimization, generation procedures and reward formulations in Section 2 and Appendix E are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ESCI and Amazon-C4 product-search coverage, Amazon Beauty sequential recommendation, ESCI re-ranking, and generalization and IR benchmarks in Appendices E.4–E.5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every reported experiment, including the retrieval baselines, SASRec/UniSRec, Qwen3-Reranker, rejection sampling/DPO, and the query-rewriting and RL-for-search comparisons in Appendix E.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain identical data splits, sample sizes, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, candidate-selection procedures and checkpoint-selection rules.

E4.justification: The prompt-design analysis, backbone comparisons, SFT-format ablations, generalization evaluations, multi-objective reward analysis and qualitative case studies in Appendices E and G are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. The same point estimates are retained, with no additions or revisions to run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance testing.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports 33.89 NDCG@100 for Rec-R1-3B+BM25 on Video Games in both versions; the supplementary results and case-study outcomes also remain identical.

T1.justification: Section 2's mathematical formulation and SFT convergence fact are unchanged, as are Appendix C's KL performance bound, RL-versus-SFT theorem, assumptions and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about closed-loop RL, avoiding synthetic SFT data, recommendation improvements and preservation of general capabilities. The added availability sentence does not revise these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning generalization, weaker transductive sequential performance, initialization dependence and historical-log feedback remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices E–F.

D1.justification: v4 adds an abstract sentence stating that data and code are available and providing the Rec-R1 repository address. v3 contains implementation details but no corresponding project-access pointer; its GitHub link concerns VeRL. Other reproducibility information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion in Appendix B are identical. No cited works or substantive research-positioning arguments are added, removed or revised.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one availability sentence, and the arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 15 October 2025 to v4 dated 28 January 2026. The remaining prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and twenty tables retain their formatting, captions and placement. The added abstract sentence fits on the existing final line, without changing the page layout.

improvement.justification: The new abstract statement gives readers an explicit location for the work's data and code, improving resource-access documentation over v3. This is a limited benefit: the scientific evidence is unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
